clue.text: The way beer gets past its best

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street, a way or road
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone notes that beer left standing goes flat and loses its quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or drink that has lost its freshness through age is described this way.

clue.text: A race to get half anti-aircraft into position for assault

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: half says only the first half of the word for anti-aircraft fire is kept

parts.note: ack-ack is old military slang for anti-aircraft fire

explanation.surface: An instruction to get anti-aircraft guns in place for an offensive during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: ACK-ACK, from the old signallers' alphabet name for AA, is halved by 'half' to ACK.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent onslaught, the same as an offensive strike on an enemy.

clue.text: She barely finishes her act

parts.note: a performer whose routine ends with her wearing next to nothing, 'barely' meaning nearly naked rather than only just

explanation.definitionFit: A performer who removes clothes for an audience ends her routine almost nude.

clue.text: Soldier in woman's clothes — then with nothing on!

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A trooper dressed as a woman and then stripped bare, a farcical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, a type of cavalry trooper.

clue.text: A chap with no hair should duck!

definitions.meaning: a man whose head is completely bald
the American wigeon, a dabbling waterfowl, is known by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a bald-headed man and is also the name of a North American wigeon.

clue.text: Traps lice by spreading dust

indicators.note: spreading the letters out and around means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone catches lice by scattering powder over them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust consists of tiny specks of matter.

clue.text: Legal tale involving a king of Egypt

indicators.note: involving means the word for tale wraps around the pharaoh's name

parts.note: a story is a tale
Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh, is known as King Tut

explanation.surface: A lawful-sounding account concerning an Egyptian pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: Something required or permitted by statute law is lawful.

clue.text: Commonplace to forbid a first lover

parts.note: to ban is to forbid

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of lover is taken

explanation.surface: It is ordinary to bar someone's first boyfriend or girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something ordinary, trite and unoriginal.

clue.text: Pop group excluded from audition

indicators.note: audition is the act of hearing, so the word is taken as heard, not as written

parts.note: someone excluded is barred or prohibited

explanation.surface: A pop group is turned away after trying out for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' wants to mean a tryout, but here it is just hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of musicians who play popular music together.

clue.text: A pretext to meet carol is agreeable

parts.note: a plea is an excuse or pretext
to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: An excuse to go carolling is a welcome one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean giving pleasure or satisfaction.

clue.text: No place for applause when one examines accounts

indicators.note: no means the abbreviation for place is removed from the word for applause

parts.note: plaudits are expressions of applause or praise
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: An accountant at work gets no clapping for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: These are official inspections of a company's books, the occasions when finances are checked.

clue.text: Don't go to the hop!

definitions.meaning: to miss or deliberately avoid attending something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to absent oneself from something and a small springing jump.

clue.text: One less regulation on guns

indicators.note: less means the letter for one is taken away from the word for regulation

parts.note: an ordinance is an authoritative rule or regulation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rule reduced by one, concerning firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery and military weaponry collectively go by this name.

clue.text: People on a fixed course

definitions.meaning: a group of people sharing descent or ethnicity
a channel or set track along which something runs, such as a millstream

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an ethnic group and also a set channel, as in a mill's water channel.

clue.text: Legal right which only one hospital has in town

parts.note: droit is a legal right, from the French word for right

indicators.note: only one says the word which, which holds two of the letter for hospital, keeps just one of them

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A town where just one hospital holds a legal entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'which' as a pronoun; it is the fodder, and 'only one hospital has' means it keeps a single one of its two Hs. Droitwich is a spa town in Worcestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Droitwich Spa is a town in Worcestershire known for its brine baths.

clue.text: Back before volcano…

indicators.note: back means the word for before is read from end to start

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: Introducing a volcano, continued into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian mountain is Europe's most famous active volcano.

clue.text: Ruler of part of east sarawak

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ruler of the eastern part of Sarawak, in Borneo.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Russian emperor, an autocratic monarch.

clue.text: …crest erupts, sucking soldiers into cavities

indicators.note: sucking means the scrambled letters draw in the soldiers
erupts means the letters of crest burst out into a new order

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: The volcano's crest blows, drawing troops into its holes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this to the volcano clue before it, so 'crest' and 'erupts' feel like scenery; 'erupts' is the anagram signal and 'sucking' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowl-shaped hollows, such as the mouths of volcanoes, are pits or cavities.

clue.text: The cat turns and I turn, not wishing to talk

indicators.note: turns means the word cat is turned around

explanation.surface: Pet and owner both turn away, wanting no conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'cat' is turned by 'turns', giving TAC; I and TURN are taken as they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is reserved and says little.

clue.text: Watch out! The fellows are troglodytes!

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, old British schoolboy slang for a lookout's warning
men are fellows

explanation.surface: A warning cry that the blokes are lurking primitive cave-dwellers.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (pronounced 'kay-vee') was shouted by British public schoolboys to warn that a teacher was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Troglodytes are prehistoric people who lived in caves.

clue.text: Viewpoint that's just a pose

definitions.meaning: a settled way of thinking about something
a posture or stance of the body

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an outlook or opinion and a physical stance or posture.

clue.text: Egg on to have a flutter

parts.note: a flutter is British slang for a small wager

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone to place a small wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite or encourage someone, usually to do wrong.

clue.text: Knocks about, worn out by drink

parts.note: beat is informal for exhausted
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A drunk, exhausted by drinking, roughs someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to assault someone violently and repeatedly.

clue.text: A little drink from a can when truce is arranged

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: is arranged means the letters of truce are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A small tipple from a can once peace terms have been agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocularly, a small measure of alcoholic spirit is called this.

clue.text: Could be sued or exploited

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone taken advantage of might also face legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taken advantage of has been made use of selfishly.

clue.text: Unions to fold if 1000 join

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the federation of British trade unions
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: Trade unions are set to collapse if a thousand members sign up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat or folded-in gather of fabric, as in dressmaking.

clue.text: They look after the queen's vehicle first

indicators.note: first means the vehicle comes at the front of the answer, before the royal part

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the queen, plus the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: They tend to the monarch's car before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people who tend and nurse others, such as the sick or elderly.

clue.text: Turn aside from composer

definitions.meaning: to deflect a blow or a question
Sir Hubert ..., English composer of the hymn Jerusalem

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to ward off a thrust, and is the surname of the English composer of Jerusalem.

clue.text: When hit, man needs bandage

parts.note: to swat is to hit sharply
he is a male person

explanation.surface: A man struck down needs dressing for his wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of fabric used for wrapping, such as a dressing, goes by this name.

clue.text: Teacher, one for a Latin lesson

parts.note: a tutor is a teacher
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A teacher signs up one pupil for Latin classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-group teaching session given by a tutor is a kind of class.

clue.text: Needless public alarm one cares about

indicators.note: about means the letters of cares are moved round into another order

explanation.surface: A widespread panic that someone frets over.
explanation.definitionFit: A widespread panic, often unwarranted, about some supposed threat.

clue.text: They make their victims late

parts.note: 'late' means dead rather than tardy, so these are people who kill others

explanation.definitionFit: Killers render their victims deceased, the late Mr So-and-so.
